name: Keep Right (island symbol)
spec: white vertical rectangle with a black arrow curving to the right of a black vertical bar
meaning: Pass to the right of the island or divider ahead.

snippets.back: Roundabout traffic travels counterclockwise around a central island, and entering traffic must yield to traffic already circulating.
Yellow left edge lines sometimes appear on divided roads where traffic cannot pull fully off, and yellow also marks obstructions and islands, which you must pass on the right.
A roundabout is an intersection arranged around a central island, with traffic traveling around that island.
A roundabout is a circular intersection where traffic moves almost nonstop in one direction around a central island.
On the freeway, signal at least two hundred feet before a lane change, avoid changing lanes often, and never drive across, over or inside a median or island.
One-way boards chain drivers to the arrow’s heading, lane-use boards bless each lane’s allowed move, and keep-right boards steer wheels past islands, medians and mid-road blocks to the shown side.
A keep-right indication directs traffic to the shown side of an island, median or obstruction.
The continued prohibition list includes the space between a safety island or zone and the curb, plus the area within thirty feet of its end unless posted otherwise.

result.summary: Snippets direct traffic to pass islands/medians on the shown/right side, supporting meaning; no snippet describes shape, color, or legend.
